title: Akron vs. Eastern Michigan — Football (2026)
location: InfoCision Stadium — Summa Health Field, Akron, Ohio
summary: Eastern Michigan edged Akron 25–23 on a late 48-yard field goal in a dramatic Homecoming finish. Original game photography by Jake Perry (@jp_sportspics).
article_headline: Eastern Michigan Stuns Akron 25–23 on Late Field Goal in Homecoming Heartbreaker
article_dek: Rudy Kessinger's 48-yard field goal with 1:50 remaining sealed a two-point MAC victory after Akron rallied to reclaim the lead in the fourth quarter.
article_body:
AKRON, Ohio — The Akron Zips looked set to deliver a Homecoming comeback at InfoCision Stadium on Saturday, October 10, but Eastern Michigan answered with the final points of a dramatic Mid-American Conference contest. A 48-yard field goal by Rudy Kessinger with 1:50 remaining lifted the Eagles to a 25–23 victory.

Akron quarterback Brayden Roggow threw for 229 yards and three touchdowns, including first-half scoring passes of 15 and 40 yards to Marcel Williams. The Zips carried a 14–13 advantage into halftime and led 17–16 entering the final quarter.

The game swung again early in the fourth when Eastern Michigan quarterback Noah Kim connected with Harold Mack for a six-yard touchdown. Down 22–17, Akron responded with a 92-yard drive capped by Roggow's 27-yard touchdown pass to Marquese Williams. That score put the Zips back in front, 23–22, with 6:27 remaining.

Eastern Michigan methodically moved into field-goal range, and Kessinger delivered the winning kick. Akron drove deep into Eagles territory in the final minute, but Matthew Schramm's potential winning 47-yard attempt missed with 19 seconds left.

Running back Jordan Gant powered Akron with 117 rushing yards, while Marcel Williams caught five passes for 89 yards and two touchdowns. Eastern Michigan's Kim passed for 277 yards, and Joshua Long made nine catches for 114 yards. The Eagles improved to 4–3 overall and 3–0 in MAC play; Akron fell to 1–5 and 0–2 in the conference.

Summit County Sports' curated photo essay captures the intensity of the afternoon from the field, photographed by Jake Perry (@jp_sportspics).

article_highlights: Rudy Kessinger connected on a 48-yard field goal with 1:50 left to give Eastern Michigan the 25–23 win.
Brayden Roggow threw three touchdown passes and 229 yards for Akron.
Marquese Williams' 27-yard touchdown reception gave Akron a 23–22 lead with 6:27 remaining.
Akron's last-second 47-yard field-goal attempt missed with 19 seconds on the clock.
Jordan Gant rushed for 117 yards; Joshua Long caught nine passes for 114 yards for Eastern Michigan.
